title: LedgerMath data API, version 1: the table of contents
description: v1/index.json: where the list of Series, the price files, the schemas, the evidence and the docs are. Start here. Every address a reader needs is written in the files, so a reader never builds one from an id; the one exception is a blob named by hash inside a Run file, whose address is evidence.blob_url_template. Version 1 only ever gains fields: a field, once in a v1 file, keeps its name, its type and its meaning, and a reader ignores any field it does not know. That is why no object in this schema, nor in series-list, series and series-month, forbids members it does not list. A change that would break a reader is published as v2, beside v1. The price files are the exception: each is the day's price file as LedgerMath keeps it, byte for byte, and follows its own schema, ledgermath.prices/1, whose root and LedgerMath's own objects are closed.

schema.description: What this file is, and which version of its shape.

about.description: What LedgerMath and this API are, in words.

versioning.description: The rule the API's own v1 files keep, in words: v1 only ever gains fields; and its exception, the price files, which follow their own schema, closed.

figures.description: How the numbers are written, in words: exactly as the Derivations hold them, never rounded.

months.description: How each Series is split by month, in words, and exactly when a month file's bytes change: for a given layout, for four causes only, a past month included, so a reader holding a copy compares the month file's sha256, which the Series' file gives, before trusting it; and what a reader does when a month file it fetched does not match its Series file.

layout.description: How the files are written, as a number. It increases when LedgerMath changes how the files are written (the order of a file's fields, the white space between them, a field every file of a kind gains), so that any file's bytes may change without one of the four causes months gives; for a given layout, those four are the only causes. Editing a schema's words does not change it, nor do the data. A reader holding copies of month files made under another layout fetches them again.

docs.description: Where the API is described in words: an absolute https address with a host, and a path, query or fragment if any, written with the characters RFC 3986 allows.

newest_run_started_at.description: When the newest Run of any Series started (UTC, to the nanosecond, as the Run records it): how far the data reach. Null when there is no Series. No file of the API carries the time it was made; the same data give the same bytes.

url.description: v1/series.json: one row per Series, each with the address of its own file.

series_file_schema_url.description: The schema of one Series' file, v1/series/<id>.json: its summary, its newest Runs and its months.

month_file_schema_url.description: The schema of one month of a Series, v1/series/<id>/<yyyy-mm>.json: every point of the Runs that started that month. A Series' file gives the address, sha256 and size of each of its months; months, above, says when a month file changes.

prices.description: The daily price files: what AWS publicly charges for what LedgerMath measures, one file a day, each byte for byte as LedgerMath keeps it. A price is cited by the price file's path (path), the SKU and the rate code.

schema_url.description: The schema of a price file (ledgermath.prices/1). A price file is a record, closed by its own schema.

newest.description: The newest price file, or null when there is none.

files.description: Every price file held, oldest first.

schemas.description: The JSON schema of each kind of file in v1.

describes.description: The files it describes, by path from the host's root.

evidence.description: Where the evidence behind the numbers is: Run files, boot summaries and blobs, served under the same address as the API, never copied into its files.

blob_url_template.description: A blob's address: replace {hex} with the 64 hex digits of a sha256:<hex> a Run file names (its binary, source, runner, stdout, stderr, dump indexes and their sections).

date.description: The UTC date the prices were fetched.

path.description: The price file's own path, prices/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/aws.json: the name a price citation gives it.
